definitions.explanation: Words or manner of speaking that invites being disliked; speaking in a way that annoys or antagonizes others.

examples.japanese: {憎|にく}まれ{口|ぐち}を{叩|たた}く。
{彼|かれ}はまた{憎|にく}まれ{口|ぐち}を{叩|たた}いて{皆|みんな}を{怒|おこ}らせた。
examples.english: He made sarcastic remarks again and angered everyone.

examples.japanese: {憎|にく}まれ{口|ぐち}ばかり{言|い}っていると、{本当|ほんとう}に{嫌|きら}われるよ。
examples.english: If you keep making harsh remarks, people will really start to dislike you.

notes:
COMMON EXPRESSION:
・{憎|にく}まれ{口|ぐち}を{叩|たた}く - to make spiteful/sarcastic remarks

PROVERB:
・{憎|にく}まれっ{子|こ}{世|よ}にはばかる - The hated child prospers in the world (troublemakers often succeed)

NOTE ON CONSTRUCTION:
{憎|にく}まれ (passive of {憎|にく}む "to hate") + {口|ぐち} (mouth/speech) = literally "speech that makes one hated"

RELATED:
・{皮肉|ひにく} - sarcasm, irony
・{嫌味|いやみ} - snide remark, sarcasm
・{毒舌|どくぜつ} - sharp tongue, caustic speech
